findings.evidence: The prior-path probe wraps its body in try/finally and calls os.close directly for every held directory FD. The parent lease setup repeats the same bare finally close loop. If body failure P is followed by close failure S, the escaping exception is S, so the outer run handler records S as primary. The first failed close also aborts the remaining close loop; these local fds are not retained in science_directory/run_directory/retained/observation for P09. Python implicit __context__ does not preserve P as the required primary or establish that later closes were attempted.
findings.impact: Violates original CP12/CP15 first-primary, ordered-secondary and known descriptor-cleanup obligations on an explicit admitted close-error branch. This rejection is conditional source control flow; no fault was injected or runtime failure claimed.
findings.minimum_resolution: Use the existing source-owned raw first-primary/secondary pattern for both preflight descriptor domains, attempt every known close independently, and keep failed/unknown cleanup non-successful while propagating the original raw primary.
findings.title: Bare preflight finally cleanup can replace the first failure and skip remaining closes
